findings.reason: without a control that can fail the node's whole measure rests on a suite that may pass on unfixed code, and the plan has to state what a non-reproducing base means (a blocker reported, not a passing arm) before a worker can close it.
findings.text: §8's negative control reads "the base revision, where a write appears after exit in at least one stage, or the test records that none does", so a base that never exhibits the defect satisfies the control and the node goes green without showing its kill handling suppresses anything — and the section's own Why says "Whether each commit postdates the signal is not yet measured", so the plan already suspects the base may not reproduce

findings.reason: one verdict would have to close both surfaces, and a worker that implements the "or" branch alone will read a done-when it cannot satisfy, costing a repair round.
findings.text: §7's deliverable says a promotion "ends with its reviewed head merged, or names the pending landing, when it will be retried, and the command that finishes it", an alternative, while its done-when requires both the merged head on the primary branch after the next landing pass and the output naming the pending landing and the finishing command, so the node carries two independently closable deliverables: the landing pass finishing the merge in `pending_landing.py`, and a new report of retry time and finishing command in `promotion.py`

findings.reason: §8's one-line invocation is lost from the chain, and §8's evidence would ride into a §7 node's dispatch, so a coordinator cannot reach §8 after §7 lands.
findings.text: f-alnw-004 carries the title "Build §7–§8" and the body "killed promotions went on committing", which is §8's defect, while `data-recommends-skill` and the prompt name only `/reckon-build a-landing-never-waits-on-a-shared-index §7`, so §8 has no invocation of its own and a node dispatched from this followup is pointed at §7 while briefed with §8's evidence

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — `reckon/crew/promotion.py:236` lands on the refusal message, imas-efit `a0cbeacc1` and `bc2183640` resolve on `origin/develop`, and all four §8 commits resolve as the promote and release commits of the two named runs.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §8's negative control admits the case where the base revision shows no post-exit write, so it passes whether or not the defect reproduces.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — both sections put their logs under the run directory and name the all_debug partition for the heavy arms, so no gate log depends on a scratchpad.
rubric_items.naming: pass — §7 and §8 introduce no plan labels, ticket numbers or version tags, and name no changelog prose.
rubric_items.reasoning: pass — §7's premise was checked in code and reproduces (the pending-landing pass iterates the pending directory while the marker is written only to the pointer), and §8 offers its unmeasured cause as a hypothesis its endpoint covers either way.
rubric_items.single_goal: a finding — §7's deliverable offers two endings while its done-when requires both, so it carries the landing pass's merge and a new pending-landing report as separate closable deliverables.
rubric_items.wiring: a finding — f-alnw-004 is titled and bodied for §7–§8 but its only invocation names §7, so §8 has no next-one-line prompt.
